primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to diabetic-hypertensive nephropathy
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) & NICE NG107 (Renal replacement therapy and conservative management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily (titrate by 2.5 mg every 2‑4 weeks to target 10 mg daily as tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade to slow CKD progression and control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile review at 6 months then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CVD risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients

medications.dose: 5 mg orally once daily (increase to 10 mg if BP target not met)
medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve target BP in proteinuric CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 BP target <130/80 mmHg when ACR ≥50 mg/mmol; CCB is recommended add‑on

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily (adjust based on volume status, may increase to 40 mg BID)
medications.duration: Lifelong — adjust as needed for fluid overload
medications.purpose: Management of volume overload and edema common in stage 4 CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG107 advises loop diuretic for fluid control in advanced CKD

medications.duration: Until ferritin >200 µg/L and TSAT >20 %, then reassess
medications.purpose: Correct iron deficiency before considering ESA therapy
medications.nice_justification: NG107 iron supplementation indicated when ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20 %

medications.dose: As currently prescribed (dose to be reviewed based on glucose logs and renal function)
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control in diabetes with CKD
medications.nice_justification: CKD guideline recommends individualized glucose control; insulin is appropriate when eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.duration: Continue — monitor electrolytes; consider switch to loop diuretic if efficacy wanes
medications.nice_justification: Thiazide may be less effective <eGFR 30 but can be used with close monitoring per NG203

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for additive effect on potassium (ACE‑I raises K⁺, thiazide can cause hypokalaemia); net effect usually neutral but requires monitoring.
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium 1‑2 weeks after starting Ramipril and after any dose change.

interactions_checked.interaction: Opposing effects on potassium (ACE‑I ↑K⁺, loop diuretic ↓K⁺); risk of dys‑kalaemia.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine after initiation and after dose adjustments.

interactions_checked.interaction: No significant pharmacokinetic interaction; watch for additive hypotension if volume depleted.
interactions_checked.action: Assess blood pressure after starting both agents.

contraindications.reason: eGFR 13.6 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the NICE TA775 threshold of ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m².
contraindications.alternative: Do not prescribe; focus on ACE‑I, BP control, and statin.

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis.
contraindications.alternative: Insulin therapy already in use; avoid metformin.

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 4; NSAIDs accelerate renal decline and cause fluid retention.
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain; avoid NSAIDs.

contraindications.reason: Guideline contraindication due to increased hyperkalaemia and AKI risk.
Risk of hyperkalaemia in CKD with ACE‑I therapy.

treatment_summary: Initiate renin‑angiotensin blockade with ramipril, add a high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin) and a calcium‑channel blocker (amlodipine) to achieve BP <130/80 mmHg. Introduce furosemide for volume control and prescribe oral iron pending iron studies. Continue current insulin and thiazide while monitoring electrolytes, renal function, and blood pressure. Avoid SGLT2 inhibitors, metformin, NSAIDs, and dual RAAS blockade. Arrange urgent labs, BP measurement, and referrals to nephrology, dietetics, and addiction services.
